structure: Part 6, place of destination and consignor pickers. Read in full: the shared picker helpers in journeys/linear/features/address-book-picker/ (address-lines.js 30 lines, render.js 80, pagination.js 91, view-model.js 62); the place-of-destination feature (page.js, evaluation.js, fields.js, controller.js 146, template.njk 117, copy/copy.en.js 67, copy/copy.cy.js 60, view-model/index.js, view-model/pagination.js, place-of-destination.fit.spec.js 505 lines with 20 tests in 5 describe blocks); the consignor-select feature (page.js, evaluation.js, fields.js, controller.js 128, template.njk 117, copy/copy.en.js 30, copy/copy.cy.js 31, view-model/index.js, view-model/pagination.js, consignor-select.fit.spec.js 498 lines with 21 tests in 5 describe blocks); and obligations/sections/destination.js (one obligation). The two pages are the same address-book picker surface: one form with a search box and secondary Search submit, a results table of radios (one page of the organisation's address book), a Selected address inset, View details disclosures, govukPagination links and the shared three save actions. They differ only in route, field name, heading and description (destination picks one of three by arrival state; consignor has one), copy, and a scope guard the consignor page has and the destination page does not. The two templates differ only in the radio name and error id. Claims run: shared picker behaviour, place of destination page, consignor page, the destination obligation, then each fit test. The address-book page size (5) is read from services/address-book/index.js, which the fit specs import, not from a file in this part's read list. Unit tests (*.test.js) are out of scope and not read.

claims.statement: Each address-book picker page shows a search box labelled 'Search' with the hint 'Name, address or country'.
The search box is a two-thirds-width text input with id and name 'q', pre-filled with the current search term.
claims.quote:
id: "q",
      name: "q",
      classes: "govuk-!-width-two-thirds",
      label: { text: copy.search.label, classes: "govuk-label--s" },
      hint: { text: copy.search.hint },
      value: picker.query

claims.statement: A secondary 'Search' button submits the same form with action 'search'.
The whole picker page is one form: the Search button and the primary save are both submits told apart by their action value, and paging is a link, so the picker needs no client-side JavaScript.
claims.quote:
The whole page is one form. The search button and the primary are both
 * submits, told apart by their `action` value, and paging is a link — so the
 * picker needs no client JavaScript at all.

claims.statement: Running a search always shows the first page of results, whichever page it was run from, and keeps the row already ticked.
The picker searches the signed-in user's organisation's address book, scoped by organisation id, for one page of results matching the search term.
claims.quote:
const orgId = organisationIdOf(request)
  const found = await addressBook.search(orgId, { query, page: pageNumber })

claims.statement: The picker shows 5 address-book records per page.
claims.ref: src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:10 (imported as PAGE_SIZE by both fit specs)

claims.statement: When the search finds records, they are shown in a table captioned 'Showing <shown> of <total> addresses'.
The results table has five columns: a visually hidden 'Select' column of radios, 'Name', 'Address', 'Country', and a visually hidden 'Actions' column holding a View details disclosure.
claims.quote:
table: {
    selectHidden: 'Select',
    name: 'Name',
    address: 'Address',
    country: 'Country',
    actionsHidden: 'Actions'
  }

claims.statement: Each row's radio is a small radio whose accessible label is visually hidden and reads 'Select <record name>'.

The Address column shows the record's address as one comma-separated line of address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postal or ZIP code, leaving out empty parts and the country, which has its own column.
claims.quote:
const ADDRESS_PARTS = [
  'addressLine1',
  'addressLine2',
  'townOrCity',
  'county',
  'postalOrZipCode'
]

/** The address as one line for the results table. The country has its own
 * column, so it is left out here. */

claims.statement: Each row has a 'View details' disclosure whose summary reads 'View details' plus a visually hidden 'for <record name>'.
The View details disclosure lists, one line each, the record's name, every address part, the country, the telephone number and the email address, leaving out any that are empty.
claims.quote:
return [
    record.name,
    ...ADDRESS_PARTS.map((part) => address[part]),
    address.country,
    address.telephoneNumber,
    address.emailAddress
  ].filter(Boolean)

claims.statement: The first row's radio on every page takes the field name as its id, so the error summary link always moves focus to the first choosable row; later rows are numbered by their position in the whole result set so ids stay distinct across pages.
A row's radio is pre-ticked when its record is the one currently selected.
When the search finds nothing, the page shows 'No addresses match your search.' instead of a table.
When a record is selected, an inset text above the results reads 'Selected address: <record name>'.
The selected record travels in a hidden 'selected' form field, so a selection made on another page of results survives a search or save from this page.

A selection counts only if the address book still holds the record: a missing or soft-deleted record is treated as no selection, and is neither shown as 'Selected address' nor carried in the paging links.
claims.quote:
A selection resolves only to a record the book still holds: a missing or
 * soft-deleted id is treated as no selection, the same way a stored reference
 * to a deleted record reads as never entered.

claims.statement: If the address book is unavailable, the picker fails with an error rather than treating the selection as deleted.
claims.quote:
An outage is not that — the
 * address book throws and the throw propagates, because an unavailable service
 * must never be indistinguishable from a deletion.

claims.statement: Pagination appears only when the search found two or more pages of results.
Pagination shows numbered links for the first page, the last page and the pages either side of the current one, with an ellipsis for any gap, and marks the current page.
claims.quote:
/** First, last, and the page either side of the current one — anything the gap
 * skips over becomes an ellipsis. */

claims.statement: Pagination shows a 'Previous' link except on the first page and a 'Next' link except on the last page.

Each paging link is a GET link to the picker page carrying the search term (q), the page number (page) and the ticked record (selected) in the query string, so a row ticked on one page is not lost on paging.
claims.quote:
Paging is a link, not a submit, so everything the next page needs travels
 * in the query string: the search term, the page and the row the trader has
 * already ticked. Without the selection a trader who picks a row on page one
 * and then pages loses it.

claims.statement: On a GET the picker reads the search term, page and selection from the q, page and selected query parameters; a missing or non-numeric page means page 1, and with no selected parameter the previously saved record is pre-selected.
claims.quote:
query: request.query.q ?? '',
    page: parsePageNumber(request.query.page),
    selectedId: request.query.selected ?? committedId(current.answers)

claims.statement: The picker pages' Back link goes to the notification's task list (overview).
The picker pages use the wider 'display' content column rather than the standard two-thirds question column.
claims.note: What the 'display' surface class renders as lives in shared/kit.js, outside this part; the statement assumes it is the wide layout its name implies.

claims.statement: Each picker page shows its section caption above the heading, then the heading as an h1 and a description paragraph under it.
Each picker page ends with the shared save actions: 'Save and continue' (action 'save'), 'Save and return to overview', and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the task list.
claims.note: Button wording comes from shared copy (another part); the fit specs name the three controls saveAndContinue, saveAndReturnToHub and cancelAndReturnToHub.

claims.statement: When the save is refused, an inline error message (with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix) appears above the results table, and the error summary is shown at the top of the page.
The error summary link moves focus to the first results row when there are results, or to the search box when the search found nothing.
Saving with no record selected, or with a record the address book no longer holds, is refused with HTTP 400, the selection cleared, and the search term and page kept.
If saving the selection fails, the picker page is shown again with the record still selected and the shared recoverable-error message, with HTTP 500.
claims.note: The recoverable-error wording is in the shared layout, another part.

claims.statement: A successful save redirects to the next page in the journey flow, worked out from the notification's scope after the save.

A picker saves only a reference to the address-book record ({ addressId }), never a copy of the address, so a record later corrected in the address book is corrected on the notification, and a deleted record stops resolving rather than leaving a stale copy.
claims.quote:
The answer stored is the address-book id and nothing else. The details are
 * resolved from the book on every read, so a record the trader later corrects
 * is corrected on the notification too, and a record they delete stops
 * resolving rather than leaving a stale copy behind.

claims.statement: Neither picker page offers a link to add a new address to the address book, or to edit one; a trader can only choose from records already in the organisation's address book.
claims.note: Looked in both templates, both copy files and both controllers: no add-address or manage-address link or route. The partition's covers names 'links to add an address'; none exists.

claims.statement: The place of destination page is at /notifications/<reference>/destinations/select.
The place of destination page collects one answer, placeOfDestination, which fulfils the placeOfDestination obligation.

The place of destination page asks one of three questions: the potato question when arrival status is not in the notification's scope, the already-arrived question when arrival status is 'already arrived', and the not-yet-arrived question otherwise, including when arrival status has not been answered yet.
Potatoes are never asked whether the consignment has arrived, because reg 24A gives them no post-arrival branch, so a potato notification always gets the pre-arrival place of destination question.
claims.quote:
Potatoes are never asked whether the consignment has arrived — reg 24A gives
 * them no post-arrival branch — so the commodity type decides the state for
 * them; plants and wood take theirs from the answer given on arrival-status.

For potatoes and for a consignment not yet arrived, the description reads 'Where the goods will be kept after arrival. This is where a plant health inspector may carry out a spot check.'

claims.statement: The place of destination is one mandatory notification-level answer for every commodity type and is never a gate: reg 24A(2)(c) asks potatoes for their intended destination and reg 26(2)(b) asks plants and wood for the intended destination or the current location.
The placeOfDestination obligation has id 7eb0d717-f852-43f7-9377-c6a9c301d702 and status mandatory.
Which of the three place of destination sentences a notifier sees is the page's choice from the arrival status, not part of the obligation.
The consignor page is at /notifications/<reference>/consignors/select.
The consignor page collects one answer, consignor, which fulfils the consignor obligation.
